# Linkgress ORM

> The ORM built for agents — AI-first by design. Linkgress is a type-safe PostgreSQL ORM for TypeScript whose query API, inferred result types and documentation are built so that an AI coding agent picks the most efficient query for a data need on the first try, and the TypeScript compiler checks every query it writes.

How to use these docs: look the data need up in Choosing the Right Query (golden rules, then decision tables: need → call → SQL shape → round trips → what to avoid, each row linking the guide section with every option), check the exact method name and the object that has it in the API Index, then copy from the linked guide section. Every page opens with a "For agents" block (the question it answers, when to use it, where to look instead, key APIs and, on most pages, their round trips) and ends with See also; pitfalls are listed as Don't → Do. SQL blocks are the statements the library sent when the example ran: one statement is one round trip (on `PostgresClient` an unnamed statement with parameters takes 2 network exchanges; see Database Clients), `$n` are bound parameters and `-- params:` lists their values; a block that could not be captured is labeled `illustrative (not captured)`. Examples use the example model `AppDatabase` (users, posts, orders, tasks, products, tags, carts and their relations); its tables, columns, relations, indexes and seed rows are in docs/example-model.md (its source, `debug/schema/appDatabase.ts`, is in the GitHub repository, not in the package).

These docs ship inside the npm package and match the installed version: `node_modules/linkgress-orm/llms.txt` (this file) and `node_modules/linkgress-orm/docs/`. Source, issues and changelogs: https://github.com/brunolau/linkgress-orm

## Start here

- [Choosing the Right Query](docs/choosing-the-right-query.md): read this first when you know what data a task needs but not which linkgress-orm call reads or writes it in the fewest statements, before writing a loop that awaits a query or a write per row, or when reviewing data-access code for extra round trips.
- [API Index](docs/api-index.md): read this when you need the exact spelling, abridged signature or guide section of a linkgress-orm export or method, or must check that a method exists on the object you hold (table, query, select builder, grouped select, CTE root, set query, union) before writing the call.
- [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md): read this when setting up linkgress-orm for the first time: entities, a `DbContext` subclass, `getSchemaManager().ensureCreated()`, and the first typed inserts, reads, collections, joins, `groupBy`, `count`/`exists`, update/delete with their SQL.
- [Example Model and Seed Data](docs/example-model.md): read this when an example names a table, column or relation of the example model (`AppDatabase`) you need to look up, a result comment depends on the seed rows, or you want to rebuild the example database to run an example yourself.

## Guides

- [Querying](docs/guides/querying.md): read this when you need to read data and must pick the call (`toList`, `select`, `firstOrDefault`, `exists`, `count`, `countOver`, navigations, collections, joins, `groupBy`/`agg` with `g.arrayAgg`/`g.countDistinct`, `union`, raw `sql`) together with the SQL it sends and its round-trip cost.
- [Batching and Prepared Queries](docs/guides/batching-and-prepared-queries.md): read this when a screen or endpoint needs several independent reads, a page plus its total count, a union's count or first row beside other reads, or the same query run many times with different values, and you must pick the form with the fewest round trips (`QueryBatch`, futures, `FutureQueryRunner`, `prepare()`).
- [Collection Strategies](docs/collection-strategies.md): read this when choosing or overriding `collectionStrategy`, predicting the SQL and round trips of a query that projects collections, or a query with collections is slow.
- [Lateral Navigation Joins: lateralJoin()](docs/guides/lateral-navigation-joins.md): read this when a query reads few rows through a foreign key into a large table and its plan merge-joins or scans the target, or before adding or reviewing a `lateralJoin()` call.
- [Subqueries](docs/guides/subquery-guide.md): read this when you must filter, exclude or compute a value from another query inside one statement (`EXISTS`, `IN`, scalar subquery, derived-table join) and need to pick between a subquery, a join, a collection or a CTE.
- [Aliased Subquery Scopes](docs/guides/aliased-scopes.md): read this when a correlated subquery must read the outer row's own table, needs joins or an `ORDER BY` + `LIMIT 1` inside the probe, or must sit inside an `UPDATE`, a CTE body, a collection item, a `HAVING` or a `MutationBatch` row guard.
- [CTEs (WITH queries)](docs/guides/cte-guide.md): read this when one statement must compute a derived set once and read it from several places, join derived sets (FULL/RIGHT/CROSS), rank then filter, or write and read back rows in one round trip (`withMutation`, `afterMutation`, `<table>.selectFromCte`).
- [Set-returning functions](docs/guides/set-returning-functions.md): read this when a JS list, JS rows or a jsonb document must become rows in SQL (join, insert, anti-join, correlate, explode per row, group elements) with statement text independent of the data size.
- [SQL Expression Helpers](docs/guides/sql-expressions.md): read this when a query needs an SQL expression beyond a plain column (a cast, a constant vs a bound parameter, CASE, a NULL default, a string/math/date function, a JSONB read/filter/partial update, an array-column test or in-place change (`arrayAppendUnique`/`arrayRemove`), an aggregate or a window value) and you need the exact SQL it emits and the JS type it reads back.
- [Inserts, Updates, Upserts and Deletes](docs/guides/insert-update-guide.md): read this when you need to insert, upsert, merge, update or delete rows, read back generated keys or written rows, or replace a per-row write loop with one statement; also for independent writes in one `MutationBatch` (legs registered `ifFits`, a guarded `addUpdateWhereIn`), bulk-write chunk sizes per client, transactions and advisory locks.
- [Schema Configuration](docs/guides/schema-configuration.md): read this when you declare or change an entity, a `DbContext` or its `setupModel()`: choosing column types (and what int8/numeric read back as), keys, relations, the indexes your queries need, enums, custom mappers, sequences or views.
- [Migrations and Schema Management](docs/guides/migrations.md): read this when you must create tables, apply model changes to an existing database, preview a schema diff, write/run/revert migration files, or know what SQL the schema manager sends and what it never changes.
- [Installation](docs/installation.md): read this when choosing and installing the driver package, verifying an install end to end, declaring linkgress-orm in a library, or fixing missing-module and TypeScript setup errors (TS1259, TS7016, TS18048).
- [Database Clients](docs/database-clients.md): read this when choosing or configuring a `DatabaseClient`, or when you need per-query timeouts, named prepared statements, several statements in one round trip, a pinned session (`connect`/`release`), a transaction at client level, raw SQL, pool sizing/`dispose`, or a custom client.
- [Configuration and Options](docs/guides/configuration.md): read this when you set up statement or failure logging, slow-statement notices, statement timeouts, server-side prepared statements, the collection strategy, list-filter rendering (`LinkgressConfig`) or the query-build caches, or need to know which of several settings wins for a statement.
- [In-Memory Database](docs/guides/in-memory-database.md): read this when running tests or examples without a PostgreSQL server (`createInMemoryDatabase`, snapshot/restore/fork, `listen`, `startInMemoryDatabaseThread`) or when judging whether a result seen in memory holds on PostgreSQL.
- [Documentation index](docs/README.md): read this when you want a task-to-page table, or every page grouped by task (reading, writing, schema and migrations, runtime and configuration, testing without a server).

## Optional

- [Changelog](https://github.com/brunolau/linkgress-orm/tree/main/changelog): one file per version (`v1.0.33.md`, …); read this when you need to know in which version an API was added or changed (the docs mark recent additions with `since 1.0.N`).
- [Contributing](https://github.com/brunolau/linkgress-orm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): read this when you change linkgress-orm itself: development setup, the test suite (PostgreSQL, in-memory, parity), code style and how to update these docs.
